solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ten years, not extremely degenerate (8)

indicators.note: only the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'not' are taken

blocks.note: a decade is ten years
the outside letters of NOT

annotation.surface: A grumble that the last ten years have been only mildly depraved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not extremely' reads as a mild qualifier on 'degenerate', but it works on the word 'not' itself, keeping just its ends.
annotation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally degenerate, given over to self-indulgence.

entries.clue: Closing section is not applicable in dossier (6)

indicators.note: NA goes inside the word for dossier

blocks.note: a dossier is a file of documents
N/A, the standard abbreviation on forms

annotation.surface: An official notes that the closing part of a report is marked N/A in the file.
annotation.walkthrough: N/A is the tick-box abbreviation on forms; 'is' is only a link word between the definition and the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing section of a piece of music or a show.

entries.clue: Great deal, including fine attic space (4)

indicators.note: the word for 'great deal' takes F inside it

blocks.note: a lot is a great deal
F = fine, as on pencil leads

annotation.surface: An estate agent's line: a bargain that comes with a fine attic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great deal' sounds like a bargain but just means 'a lot'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the roof space of a house, reached by a hatch or ladder, goes by this name in Britain.

entries.clue: Queen referring to gain in an unusual way (6)

indicators.note: the letters of 'gain' are arranged in an unusual order

blocks.note: re = regarding, as in a letter heading
letters of GAIN rearranged

annotation.surface: A remark about the Queen profiting by odd means.
annotation.walkthrough: Regina is Latin for queen, the R in ER on British postboxes.
annotation.definitionFit: Regina is the Latin title of a reigning queen.

entries.clue: It may help to remember version adapted to accommodate you (8)

indicators.note: 'version' is changed into a new arrangement
the rearranged letters take U inside them

blocks.note: letters of VERSION rearranged
U = you, as in texting

annotation.surface: Someone making a memorable version of something, tailored to suit you.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: a souvenir is kept to help you remember a trip.
annotation.definitionFit: A souvenir is a keepsake whose job is to call a place or event to mind.

entries.clue: Cheers up over drink, with minimum of ice included, in part of large building (6)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word for cheers upside down
the first part is placed above, before, the drink
the I goes inside the drink
only the smallest part, the first letter, of 'ice' is taken

blocks.note: TA is British slang for thanks, turned upward
rum, a spirit
first letter of ICE, placed inside RUM

annotation.surface: Drinkers cheering up over a rum with a bit of ice somewhere in a grand building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' here is TA, a British way of saying thank you, not a toast; 'up' flips it because this is a down clue.
annotation.definitionFit: An atrium is the central hall or open court of a large building.

entries.clue: Brilliant to incorporate Mike’s highest point of achievement (4)

indicators.note: the word for brilliant takes M into its body

blocks.note: ace = excellent, brilliant
Mike is M in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Praise for Mike's career peak.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's in Mike's is only surface glue; M sits inside ACE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from the Greek for 'point', it names the very summit of anything, especially achievement.

entries.clue: Not quite epic — large book summary (7)

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, losing its last letter

blocks.note: EPIC without its last letter
a tome is a big, heavy book

annotation.surface: A review sneering that a big book falls short of epic.
annotation.walkthrough: Epitome is used here in its older sense of an abstract or summary, not 'perfect example'.
annotation.definitionFit: An epitome is a summary or abstract of a written work.

entries.clue: Device for measuring spirits — choose one carefully to begin with (5)

indicators.note: only the beginning, the first letter, of 'carefully' is taken

blocks.note: to opt is to choose
I = one, the Roman numeral
first letter of CAREFULLY

annotation.surface: Advice to a bar-worker to pick a measure with care.
annotation.walkthrough: An optic is the British pub device fixed to an upside-down bottle that dispenses an exact measure of spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: Optic is the trade name for the measuring tap on spirit bottles in British bars.

entries.clue: Separate answer section (5)

blocks.note: A = answer, as in Q and A
section, as in one portion of a paper

annotation.surface: An exam instruction to answer one section separately.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separate' is an adjective here, as in 'kept apart'.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, 'kept apart' and 'kept separate' mean the same thing, so the swap works.

entries.clue: Bill ready to sing? (7)

blocks.note: bill in the commercial sense, a request for payment
a singer ready to perform is said to be in good voice; here the answer splits into two words

annotation.surface: A man called Bill warming up to sing.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name, a singer; the second meaning splits the answer into IN VOICE, which the question mark flags as playful.
annotation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent for goods or work.

entries.clue: Discomfort seeing letters, we hear — practise (9)

indicators.note: the letters are heard, not seen, giving their sound

blocks.note: the letter I in the plural, said out loud
to train is to practise

annotation.surface: A complaint about the discomfort of reading, then an instruction to practise.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letters' is not any letters but specifically the letter I, twice, which sounds like EYES.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is discomfort in the eyes from seeing too hard or too long.

entries.clue: Attempt to pack in a singlet is farce (8)

indicators.note: the word for attempt packs the other words inside it

blocks.note: a try is an attempt
A + VEST, a vest being a singlet

annotation.surface: Someone trying to cram a sleeveless top into a bag, a farce.
annotation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, a singlet, not a waistcoat.
annotation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, a farce.

entries.clue: Slander most ugly, despicable, first of all (3)

indicators.note: the first letter of all three words is taken

blocks.clueFragment: most ugly, despicable, first of all
blocks.note: first letters of MOST, UGLY, DESPICABLE

annotation.surface: A verdict that slander is the ugliest, vilest thing of all.
annotation.walkthrough: The three adjectives look like a description of slander but are only there for their first letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Mud, as in 'mud-slinging', is damaging talk about someone.

entries.clue: Pay no regard to deduction from full price (8)

blocks.note: verb sense: to set aside or disregard
noun sense: money taken off the price

annotation.surface: A shopper told to ignore the reduction from the full price.
annotation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a verb, the second a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Discount means both to disregard and a price reduction.

entries.clue: Rebuke, however you look at it (3)

indicators.note: the word is the same read either way

blocks.note: the definition end: a small clicking noise of disapproval

annotation.surface: Someone insisting a telling-off is a telling-off, whatever the angle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'However you look at it' sounds like a shrug but is the whole of the wordplay: nothing is turned into anything else.
annotation.definitionFit: To tut is to make a small clicking sound of disapproval, a mild rebuke.

entries.clue: Vegetable change I propose initially (6)

indicators.note: only the initial letter of 'propose' is taken

blocks.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns
I, as written
first letter of PROPOSE

annotation.surface: Someone suggesting a change of vegetable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change' is a verb here, TURN, as leaves turn in autumn.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: this is one particular root vegetable, round with white flesh.

entries.clue: Equipment mixed up as a trap? (9)

indicators.note: the letters that follow are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Wondering whether some kit has been set up as a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of 'mixed up', but the anagram needs its letters; only 'mixed' is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the set of tools or machines used for a job, as in breathing or laboratory gear.

entries.clue: Steal from large building housing female by river (6)

indicators.note: the word for large building houses F inside it
'by' means next to, as in a house by the sea, so R stands beside the rest

blocks.note: a pile is a large, grand building
F = female
R = river, as on maps

annotation.surface: A plan to steal from a riverside mansion where a woman lives.
annotation.walkthrough: A pile is a jokey British word for a stately home.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with a flavour of petty theft: taking small items on the sly.

entries.clue: Showy stuff put in selection boxes (6)

indicators.note: the phrase boxes the answer inside it

blocks.note: inside puT IN SELection

annotation.surface: Glitzy things packed into a selection box, a Christmas scene.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' is a verb, not the selection boxes of chocolates at Christmas.
annotation.definitionFit: Tinsel is glittery decoration, showy but cheap.

entries.clue: After shake-up a ruler’s very strange (7)

indicators.note: the letters that follow have been shaken into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A political comment: after a government reshuffle the leader is behaving oddly.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's of ruler's supplies the S, and 'shake-up' sounds like a cabinet reshuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: Surreal means bizarre, dreamlike, very strange.

entries.clue: Cereal close to oats in the past (4)

indicators.note: the close, the last letter, of 'oats' is taken

blocks.note: last letter of OATS
ago = in the past

annotation.surface: A food historian saying a cereal once came close to oats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near', but it means the end of 'oats'.
annotation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy grain from palm pith, used like a cereal in puddings.

entries.clue: Part of Robin Goodfellow’s game (5)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the words that follow

blocks.note: inside roBIN GOodfellow's

annotation.surface: A question about which game belongs to Robin Goodfellow, the folklore sprite Puck.
annotation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck; the name is only there to carry the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance played with numbered cards.

entries.clue: Centre of operations of inferior quality (4)

blocks.note: the headquarters that operations are run from, as for an army
low-grade, as in the metals alchemists tried to turn to gold

annotation.surface: A complaint that headquarters is shoddy.
annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is a noun, the second an adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: Base is both a headquarters and an adjective for low or inferior.

entries.clue: Remorse of fellowship, taking time to replace diamonds (5)

indicators.note: the word for fellowship takes on a T
the T takes the place of the D

blocks.note: a guild is an association, a fellowship
T = time
D = diamonds, the card suit; this letter goes out

annotation.surface: A member of a fellowship regretting a lapse, ready to swap time for jewels.
annotation.walkthrough: GUILD loses its D, the diamonds of card-playing, and T comes in instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the bad feeling after doing wrong, close enough to remorse to swap in.

entries.clue: English at back of ship referring to One Direction? (7)

indicators.note: the E sits with the word for the back of a ship

blocks.note: E = English
astern means at or toward the rear of a ship

annotation.surface: An English fan at the back of a boat talking about the boy band One Direction.
annotation.walkthrough: One Direction is the boy band, but the definition means literally one compass direction, east.
annotation.definitionFit: Eastern means relating to the east, one of the four compass directions.
